approval_required_for: Any modification to the exact user-supplied wrapper, selected source closure, wrapper/source hashes, or AXI/DDR behavior.
Any DUT RTL hierarchy, interface, lifecycle, pipeline, memory-layout, runtime-ABI, architecture, or major template change.
Any change to checkpoint, stimulus, independent target-model reference, expected output, numeric policy, tolerance, semantic testbench contract, or required Transformer-block weight scope.

Any fallback that removes current-DAG observations, relaxes an observability or acceptance checker, replaces target-model inference, derives golden data from RTL output, or treats sampled weights as complete consumption evidence.
Any lower-layer backtrack, connected-kernel replay, or operator-leaf rerun without a new current hash-bound trace explicitly contradicting a named certified invariant.
Any promotion claim before fresh exact-board current-layer real-tool evidence and all required dependent board acceptance gates pass.
Any change to elastic variable-latency pipeline semantics, cross-token overlap requirements, or memory/data-order contracts.

executable_actions.rationale: The earliest real failure is a generated board-testbench observability XMRE before simulation. The supplied evidence has source lines and tokens but lacks declaration context and authoritative compile-order/source-hash provenance needed for a minimal legal binding. The multi-agent system has no registered compiler-provenance extractor for this capability, so planned_tool.vcs_compile_diagnostic_source_provenance and planned_checker.vcs_compile_diagnostic_source_provenance must be implemented or provided as a bounded read-only artifact producer. This action does not authorize a DUT edit, exact-wrapper edit, unchanged-source VCS replay, lower-layer replay, or runtime interpretation.

observations: The current applicability binding is for board_axi_ddr_wrapped_system and applies to case_vcs_functional_sim and case_vcs_evidence_analyzer. The first real error is Error-[XMRE] in generated spatialacc_exact_board_multilayer_tb.sv at lines 313, 316, 319, 322, 325, and 328 for six unresolved references used by current_dag_boundary_payload.

The supplied compile tail identifies the source lines and hierarchy tokens, but it does not establish the authoritative declaration or instance context for those signals or the authoritative VCS source file list and compile order. Guessing legal replacements is therefore unsafe.

Elaboration failed with returncode 1, simulation.status is not_run, the elaborated hierarchy report is invalid, and all runtime reports required for AXI protocol, pipeline overlap, loader consumption, DDR round-trip, and numeric comparison are absent. No board output-frontier or lifecycle-frontier claim is admissible.

The existing boundary_trace artifact contains observational failures, including kernel_start_to_core=0 and zero accepted egress, but the CCTG causal slice explicitly reports not_applicable_before_runtime_execution. These records cannot establish a current board-to-kernel contradiction or prove block_input is a hardware root cause while the exact-board compile has not completed.

The conditional specialist review is consistent with a provenance-first decision: acquire complete compile provenance before any source repair, and keep the repair confined to simulation/testbench observability. Removing probes, tying payloads to constants, relaxing the observability schema, guessing hierarchy names, or changing DUT ports is prohibited.

The exact user-supplied wrapper and board source identity are passing, with exact wrapper/source closure hashes bound and simulation hashes matching the selected source identity. The wrapper and its AXI/DDR behavior must remain unchanged.

The operator-leaf and connected-kernel layers have live hash-bound pass evidence. The connected-kernel capability records accepted ingress and egress counts of 1792, a direct start witness, terminal egress last, and elastic variable-latency cross-token overlap. No new current trace explicitly contradicts a named certified invariant, so those layers are closed and must not be replayed or repaired.

The target-model expected-output source is target_model_inference, but board numeric comparison did not run. Board validation currently covers only a one-layer prefix with all_target_layers=false; this is an acceptance obligation for later board closure, not authorization to change the checkpoint, stimulus, golden, tolerance, loader contract, or Transformer-block scope.

sacg_memory_truth shows active contamination barriers and eight open same-stage retry requests, with no open board-scope backtrack request. Any refined retry must produce fresh hash-bound artifacts and pass current-stage checkers before superseding prior failed artifacts or enabling promotion.

The next current-layer boundary replay is deferred, not skipped: it cannot be generated or trusted until the compile-time observability binding is provenance-resolved and a fresh exact-board tool run completes. No dependent board gate or higher layer may run now.
proposed_actions: Execute only the hash-bound read-only VCS compile-provenance acquisition. Require the resulting artifact to identify the first XMRE, all six source locations and hierarchy tokens, their declaration/instance context, the authoritative compile file list and order with source hashes, and whether a legal simulation-only bind/adapter exists. Keep functional_sim and all dependent board gates blocked until that artifact passes; do not perform the generated-source repair or any VCS rerun in this decision.
risks: A guessed replacement for any unresolved hierarchy token could compile while silently dropping or misbinding a required current-DAG boundary observation.

Deleting or zeroing current_dag_boundary_payload assignments, weakening the observability contract, or using an RTL output as a debug golden would mask a verification-capability failure rather than repair it.
Treating the pre-runtime boundary records as a board-to-kernel contradiction could incorrectly reopen the certified connected kernel and repeat closed work.

A compile-only correction cannot establish board correctness; fresh evidence is still required for lifecycle, output count and order, AXI protocol, DDR image round-trip, complete bound Transformer-block weights, and target-model numeric comparison.
Changing checkpoint, stimulus, target-model inference, numeric tolerance, semantic testbench hashes, exact wrapper/source hashes, or model-tail boundaries would contaminate the retry.
Independent AXI or prefetch activity, if later observed, must not be confused with output-frontier progress; a future runtime stall requires a fresh current board trace and causal localization.
